newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey plans 11 new hydroelectric power plants.
newsitem.headline: Turkey plans 11 new hydroelectric power plants.

text.p: The Turkish Energy Ministry has invited companies to build dams and hydroelectric power stations under a build-operate-transfer (BOT) scheme at 11 sites.
The invitation published in the official gazette on Tuesday said the capacity of the 11 stations would total 2,688 MegaWatts (MW) and would produce 9.29 billion kiloWatt-hours (kWh) a year.

The Ministry gave separate deadlines from November 18, 1996 to March 17, 1997 for companies to present feasibility studies on the projects they are interested in as well as other detailed information and letter of guarantees.

After years of self-sufficiency in power production, Turkey faced an energy shortfall this year due to a lack of investment caused by bureaucratic obstacles of the BOT system -- developed in the late 1980s to finance big infrastructure projects.

Power demand has been rising by about eight percent annually in Turkey which has a total power generation capacity of 105 billion kWh and is expected to produce 93.1 billion kWh this year against a projected consumption of 97.5 billion kWh.
Turkey derived 36 percent of its 1995 power output of 86.3 billion kWh from coal-fired plants, the rest from hydropower.
Electricity imports from Iran began in August and talks were underway with Georgian and Bulgarian companies for more imports to cover the energy deficit expected in the last quarter.
Other major power generation projects, including gas-fired and nuclear plants, are also under consideration.
